# pcmtap

Record what an app, or the whole Mac, is playing, as PCM audio. It uses Core Audio process taps (macOS 14.2+), so there is no BlackHole, no virtual device and no change to your audio routing.

```python
from pcmtap import record

record("spotify.wav", 30, app="Spotify", mute=True)   # 30 s of Spotify alone, silent on the speakers
record("everything.flac", 10)                          # whatever the Mac plays
```

```bash
pip install pcmtap
pcmtap check                                           # what is missing, with the fix
pcmtap record out.wav --seconds 30 --app Spotify --mute
pcmtap list --playing                                  # which processes are making sound
```

## The first run

The first run needs two things from macOS.

1. **The helper is built.** The real-time capture is a small Swift program shipped as source. On first use pcmtap compiles it with `swiftc` (from the Xcode command line tools: `xcode-select --install`) into `~/.local/share/pcmtap/bin/`.
2. **The permission is granted.** macOS asks once whether *pcmtap-helper* may record system audio: `pcmtap permission --request` shows the dialog. You can also allow it later in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording. Without the permission, macOS hands a tap silence rather than an error; pcmtap notices and raises `PermissionMissing`.

The helper makes itself responsible for its own privacy permissions. So the grant is remembered for pcmtap-helper, whichever terminal, IDE or detached tmux session runs it. A new pcmtap version with a changed helper asks once more.

## Choosing what to record

- `app="Spotify"` or `app="com.spotify.client"`: an app by name or bundle id. A bundle id is a prefix, so an app’s helper processes are included.
- `pid=1234`: one process. Lists work for both.
- Neither: the whole Mac. `exclude=True` records everything *except* the selection.
- `mute=True` keeps the recorded processes off the speakers while they are recorded; the recording itself stays at full level.

An app can be tapped once it has opened an audio stream (played something since it launched).

## Streaming

`Tap` is a context manager that yields chunks of interleaved float32 frames. The functions in `pcmtap.stream` compose over them:

```python
from pcmtap import Tap, skip_silence, take_seconds, write_audio

with Tap(app="Spotify", mute=True) as tap:
    fmt = tap.format                                    # AudioFormat(sample_rate=44100, channels=2)
    chunks = skip_silence(iter(tap), fmt, timeout_s=20)
    write_audio("song.flac", take_seconds(chunks, fmt, 180), fmt)
```

`.wav` is written natively (32-bit float, the exact samples). Other formats go through `ffmpeg`.

## Agents

The package ships an agent skill (`pcmtap/data/skills/pcmtap/SKILL.md`): `gh skill install thorwhalen/pcmtap pcmtap`. `CLAUDE.md` is the map for agents developing pcmtap.

<p class="epythet-aggregates">This documentation as a single file: <a href="pcmtap.md">pcmtap.md</a> (Markdown, for agents).</p>

# _autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md

# pcmtap.helper_build

Find or build the native helper (`pcmtap-helper`) that does the real-time capture.

The helper is a small Swift program shipped as source (`pcmtap/helper/`) and
compiled with `swiftc` on first use into [`helper_dir()`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.helper_dir), always at the same
path ([`HELPER_NAME`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.HELPER_NAME)), with the source’s hash in a sidecar file. A pcmtap
version whose helper source changed rebuilds it in place; any other version reuses
it. macOS keys the *System Audio Recording* permission to the binary’s path (and,
for an ad hoc signature, its contents), so the stable path is what lets an upgrade
that does not touch the helper keep the permission.

Set `$PCMTAP_HELPER` to use a helper binary built elsewhere.

### Module Attributes

| [`HELPER_NAME`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.HELPER_NAME)   | stable, because macOS keys the permission to its path.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| [`MIN_MACOS`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.MIN_MACOS)     | Process taps arrived in macOS 14.2.                      |

### Functions

| [`build_helper`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.build_helper)(target)       | Compile the helper into `target` with `swiftc` and sign it (ad hoc).             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`helper_dir`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.helper_dir)()               | Where built helpers live: `$PCMTAP_DATA_DIR/bin` or `~/.local/share/pcmtap/bin`. |
| [`helper_path`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.helper_path)(\*[, rebuild]) | The helper binary, building it first if this version has not been built yet.     |
| [`macos_version`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.macos_version)()            | This Mac's version as a tuple, or `None` when not on macOS.                      |

### Exceptions

| [`HelperUnavailable`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#pcmtap.helper_build.HelperUnavailable)   | The native helper cannot be found or built on this machine.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/pcmtap.html.md

# pcmtap

Record what an app (or the whole Mac) is playing, as PCM, via Core Audio process taps.

```pycon
>>> from pcmtap import record
>>> record("song.wav", 30, app="Spotify", mute=True)
PosixPath('song.wav')
```

For streaming, [`Tap`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.Tap) yields chunks of interleaved float32 frames, and
[`pcmtap.stream`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#module-pcmtap.stream) composes over them (skip the leading silence, take N seconds).
macOS 14.2+; the first recording asks for the *System Audio Recording* permission
([`request_permission()`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.request_permission), `pcmtap permission --request`).

### Functions

| [`audio_processes`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.audio_processes)()                               | The processes Core Audio knows: `pid`, `bundle_id`, `running_output`.                               |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.check_requirements)(\*[, request])               | Problems (each with its remedy) that stop pcmtap from recording; empty means ready.                 |
| [`helper_path`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.helper_path)(\*[, rebuild])                      | The helper binary, building it first if this version has not been built yet.                        |
| [`peak`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.peak)(chunk)                                     | The largest absolute sample in `chunk` (0.0 for an empty one).                                      |
| [`permission_status`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.permission_status)()                             | `"granted"`, `"denied"`, `"not_determined"` or `"unknown"`.                                         |
| [`record`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.record)(path[, seconds, app, pid, exclude, ...]) | Record what `app` (default: every process) plays into `path`; returns the path.                     |
| [`request_permission`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.request_permission)()                            | Ask macOS for *System Audio Recording* (a dialog on the Mac's screen); blocks until it is answered. |
| [`resolve_app`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.resolve_app)(app)                                | A bundle id (prefix) for `app`: a bundle id is kept; an app name is looked up.                      |
| [`skip_silence`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.skip_silence)(chunks, fmt, \*[, threshold, ...]) | Drop the leading silence: start at the first frame louder than `threshold`.                         |
| [`take_frames`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.take_frames)(chunks, fmt, frames)                | The first `frames` frames of the stream, then stop (the source is not drained).                     |
| [`take_seconds`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.take_seconds)(chunks, fmt, seconds)              | The first `seconds` seconds of the stream.                                                          |
| [`take_until`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.take_until)(chunks, stop)                        | Chunks until `stop()` returns true (checked before each chunk).                                     |
| [`write_audio`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.write_audio)(path, chunks, fmt, \*[, bitrate])   | Write `chunks` to `path`: natively for `.wav`, through ffmpeg otherwise.                            |
| [`write_wav`](_autosummary/pcmtap.html.md#pcmtap.write_wav)(path, chunks, fmt)                    | Write `chunks` to a 32-bit float WAV at `path`; returns the path.                                   |

# _autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md

# pcmtap.stream

Operations on a stream of PCM chunks (interleaved float32 `bytes`).

Each takes an iterable of chunks and an [`pcmtap.tap.AudioFormat`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.AudioFormat) and returns a
new iterator, so they compose: `take_seconds(skip_silence(tap, fmt), fmt, 30)`.

```pycon
>>> from pcmtap.tap import AudioFormat
>>> from array import array
>>> fmt = AudioFormat(sample_rate=4, channels=1)
>>> chunks = [array("f", [0, 0]).tobytes(), array("f", [0, .5, .5, .5]).tobytes()]
>>> b"".join(take_frames(skip_silence(chunks, fmt), fmt, 2)) == array("f", [.5, .5]).tobytes()
True
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_SILENCE_THRESHOLD`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.DEFAULT_SILENCE_THRESHOLD)   | Peak amplitude below which audio counts as silence (about -60 dBFS).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`peak`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.peak)(chunk)                                     | The largest absolute sample in `chunk` (0.0 for an empty one).                  |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`samples`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.samples)(chunk)                                  | The float32 samples in `chunk`.                                                 |
| [`skip_silence`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.skip_silence)(chunks, fmt, \*[, threshold, ...]) | Drop the leading silence: start at the first frame louder than `threshold`.     |
| [`take_frames`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.take_frames)(chunks, fmt, frames)                | The first `frames` frames of the stream, then stop (the source is not drained). |
| [`take_seconds`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.take_seconds)(chunks, fmt, seconds)              | The first `seconds` seconds of the stream.                                      |
| [`take_until`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.take_until)(chunks, stop)                        | Chunks until `stop()` returns true (checked before each chunk).                 |

### Exceptions

| [`SilenceTimeout`](_autosummary/pcmtap.stream.html.md#pcmtap.stream.SilenceTimeout)   | No sound arrived within the allowed time.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md

# pcmtap.tap

A live tap on what processes are playing: a context manager yielding PCM chunks.

```pycon
>>> with Tap(app="Spotify", mute=True) as tap:
...     print(tap.format)
...     for chunk in tap:          # bytes of interleaved float32 frames
...         ...
```

`Tap` runs the native helper ([`pcmtap.helper_build`](_autosummary/pcmtap.helper_build.html.md#module-pcmtap.helper_build)) as a subprocess and
reads its stdout. Chunks always hold whole frames.

### Module Attributes

| [`SAMPLE_FORMAT`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.SAMPLE_FORMAT)   | Sample formats the helper emits (interleaved little-endian float32).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`audio_processes`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.audio_processes)()    | The processes Core Audio knows: `pid`, `bundle_id`, `running_output`.                               |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`permission_status`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.permission_status)()  | `"granted"`, `"denied"`, `"not_determined"` or `"unknown"`.                                         |
| [`request_permission`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.request_permission)() | Ask macOS for *System Audio Recording* (a dialog on the Mac's screen); blocks until it is answered. |
| [`resolve_app`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.resolve_app)(app)     | A bundle id (prefix) for `app`: a bundle id is kept; an app name is looked up.                      |

### Classes

| [`AudioFormat`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.AudioFormat)(sample_rate, channels[, ...])   | The PCM layout of a tap's output.                                    |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Tap`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.Tap)([app, pid, exclude, mute, seconds])     | Capture what processes play, as an iterator of PCM chunks (`bytes`). |

### Exceptions

| [`PermissionMissing`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.PermissionMissing)   | macOS has not granted *System Audio Recording* to pcmtap's helper.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TapError`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.TapError)            | The helper could not start or keep the tap.                          |

### *class* pcmtap.tap.AudioFormat(sample_rate, channels, sample_format='f32le')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Sample formats the helper emits (interleaved little-endian float32).

### *class* pcmtap.tap.Tap(app=None, , pid=None, exclude=False, mute=False, seconds=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Capture what processes play, as an iterator of PCM chunks (`bytes`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **app** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – Bundle id(s) or app name(s) to record; all of their processes are
    included (`"com.spotify.client"` also matches its helper processes).
  * **pid** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – Process id(s) to record.
  * **exclude** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Record everything *except* the selected processes.
  * **mute** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Silence the recorded processes on the speakers while recording.
  * **seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Stop after this long (otherwise when closed).

With no `app` and no `pid`, records every process on the Mac.

#### close()

Stop the capture and the helper.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### open()

Start the helper and wait for it to report its audio format.

* **Return type:**
  [`Tap`](_autosummary/pcmtap.tap.html.md#pcmtap.tap.Tap)

# _autosummary/pcmtap.write.html.md

# pcmtap.write

Write a stream of PCM chunks to an audio file.

`.wav` is written natively (32-bit float WAV, the tap’s exact samples, no
dependency). Any other extension (`.flac`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.ogg`…) is
encoded by `ffmpeg` as the chunks arrive.

### Functions

| [`write_audio`](_autosummary/pcmtap.write.html.md#pcmtap.write.write_audio)(path, chunks, fmt, \*[, bitrate])   | Write `chunks` to `path`: natively for `.wav`, through ffmpeg otherwise.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`write_wav`](_autosummary/pcmtap.write.html.md#pcmtap.write.write_wav)(path, chunks, fmt)                    | Write `chunks` to a 32-bit float WAV at `path`; returns the path.          |
| [`write_with_ffmpeg`](_autosummary/pcmtap.write.html.md#pcmtap.write.write_with_ffmpeg)(path, chunks, fmt, \*[, ...]) | Encode `chunks` into `path` with ffmpeg (format from its extension).       |

### pcmtap.write.write_audio(path, chunks, fmt, , bitrate=None)

Write `chunks` to `path`: natively for `.wav`, through ffmpeg otherwise.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### pcmtap.write.write_wav(path, chunks, fmt)

Write `chunks` to a 32-bit float WAV at `path`; returns the path.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### pcmtap.write.write_with_ffmpeg(path, chunks, fmt, , bitrate=None, ffmpeg=None)

Encode `chunks` into `path` with ffmpeg (format from its extension).

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`pcmtap` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `pcmtap`

Record what an app, or the whole Mac, is playing, as PCM audio, with the pcmtap Python package or its `pcmtap` CLI (Core Audio process taps, macOS 14.2+, no BlackHole or virtual device). Use when asked to record system audio, capture an app’s sound output (Spotify, a browser, Zoom, a game), make a loopback or “what you hear” recording, tap audio from a process, get the PCM of what is playing, record a stream, mute an app while recording it, or check or grant the macOS System Audio Recording permission. Triggers on “record what’s playing”, “capture system audio”, “audio loopback on mac”, “tap Spotify’s audio”, “record app audio”, “pcmtap”.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/pcmtap pcmtap --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`pcmtap/data/skills/pcmtap`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/pcmtap/tree/HEAD/pcmtap/data/skills/pcmtap) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install pcmtap`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/pcmtap/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/pcmtap/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`pcmtap.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/pcmtap/pcmtap.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/pcmtap/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
